description: API response optimization, pagination enforcement, frontend performance (route lazy loading, component memoization, debounced search). No new state management or virtualised list libraries (react-window/react-virtual not in package.json). Independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-002.
steps: 1. Enforce max page size on DRF list views. In backend/config/settings.py, set REST_FRAMEWORK['PAGE_SIZE'] to 50 (increase from 20 for balance between UX and load), and add 'MAX_PAGE_SIZE': 100 to REST_FRAMEWORK config. Audit 10 highest-traffic list views (orders, bills, payments, inventory items, notifications, kitchen orders, menu items, customers, staff assignments, reporting exports). If any use custom pagination_class that overrides max_page_size, set it to 100.

2. Create backend/core/pagination.py with a SafePageNumberPagination class that inherits from PageNumberPagination, sets max_page_size=100, and logs a warning when a client requests page_size > max_page_size. Use this as DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS in settings.py REST_FRAMEWORK config instead of the plain PageNumberPagination.

3. Audit backend/reporting/views.py export endpoints (ExportCSVView). These return full result sets as CSV downloads — no pagination. Add a MAX_EXPORT_ROWS constant in reporting/constants.py (set to 10000). In ExportCSVView.get(), after fetching data from the service function, check if row count exceeds MAX_EXPORT_ROWS; if yes, return HTTP 400 with error message: 'Export exceeds maximum row limit. Narrow your date range or filters.' Add a query parameter max_rows for admins to override (if user has reporting.export.unlimited permission, allow up to 50000).

4. Review backend/operations/views.py (POS catalog endpoints). Ensure POS menu catalog endpoint uses the menu catalog cache from FEAT-002 (if FEAT-002 is implemented) or at minimum applies select_related/prefetch_related. If the POS view builds a large nested JSON structure, profile it in code review — if serialization is slow, switch to a flatter structure or pre-aggregate.

5. Frontend route lazy loading. Edit frontend/src/App.tsx: replace all direct page component imports (lines 7-150) with lazy-loaded imports using React.lazy(). Example: change 'import { OrganizationsListPage } from ...' to 'const OrganizationsListPage = React.lazy(() => import(...))'. Wrap the block in a Loading...}>. Group imports by feature: auth (2 pages), organizations (6 pages), users+roles (3 pages), counters (4 pages), menu (6 pages), tables+orders (4 pages), kitchen (2 pages), billing (5 pages), payments (1 page), inventory (9 pages), recipes (3 pages), central control (5 pages), notifications (2 pages), marketing (5 pages), operations (6 pages), enterprise (8 pages), crm (7 pages), reporting (8 pages), accounting (8 pages), financials (7 pages). Total ~90 lazy-loaded chunks. Keep DashboardPage, LoginPage, RegisterPage eager-loaded (frequently accessed on first visit).

6. Frontend component memoization. Identify top 5 frequently re-rendered components by inspecting props complexity: (a) frontend/src/components/orders/MenuItemCard.tsx — if it receives complex menu item props, wrap export in React.memo((props) => <MenuItemCard {...props} />, (prevProps, nextProps) => prevProps.item.id === nextProps.item.id && prevProps.item.updated_at === nextProps.item.updated_at). (b) frontend/src/components/kitchen/KitchenOrderCard.tsx — wrap in React.memo with shallow equality check on order.id and order.status. (c) frontend/src/components/ui/StatCard.tsx — if rendered in loops on dashboards, wrap in React.memo with shallow props check. (d) frontend/src/components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx — wrap in React.memo since it renders on every page via MainLayout. (e) frontend/src/components/billing/BillItemsTable.tsx — wrap in React.memo if items array reference changes frequently. Only add memoization where props change less frequently than parent re-renders. Do NOT memo components that receive new callbacks on every render (unless those callbacks are useCallback-wrapped).

7. Debounced search inputs. Create frontend/src/hooks/useDebounce.ts: export a useDebounce(value, delay=300) hook that returns the debounced value after delay ms of inactivity. Find all search input fields: (a) frontend/src/pages/menu/MenuItems.tsx — if there is a search input, wrap its value in useDebounce before passing to the API query. (b) frontend/src/pages/inventory/InventoryItemsPage.tsx — same. (c) frontend/src/pages/crm/CustomerListPage.tsx — same. (d) frontend/src/pages/orders/OrderListPage.tsx — same. (e) Any other list page with a search box. The pattern: const [search, setSearch] = useState(''); const debouncedSearch = useDebounce(search, 300); const query = useOrders({ search: debouncedSearch, ... }); <input value={search} onChange={(e) => setSearch(e.target.value)} />. This prevents firing an API request on every keystroke.

8. Audit frontend/src/hooks/ for duplicate or redundant API calls. Check: useOrders, useBills, usePayments, useMenu, useInventory, useNotifications. Ensure each uses TanStack Query's staleTime and cacheTime appropriately. Set staleTime: 30000 (30s) for relatively static data (menu, categories, branches), staleTime: 5000 (5s) for operational data (orders, bills, kitchen), staleTime: 0 for real-time data (notifications if not using WebSocket). Add these as defaults in the query client configuration in frontend/src/main.tsx: queryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 30000, cacheTime: 300000, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } } }).

9. Add loading skeletons to 3 high-traffic pages: (a) frontend/src/pages/orders/OrderListPage.tsx — render a skeleton list (5 skeleton cards) while useOrders.isLoading. (b) frontend/src/pages/kitchen/KitchenDashboard.tsx — render skeleton kitchen cards while data is loading. (c) frontend/src/pages/billing/BillListPage.tsx — render skeleton table rows. Create a reusable Skeleton component in frontend/src/components/ui/Skeleton.tsx (a simple animated div with gray gradient).

10. Frontend build optimization. Audit frontend/vite.config.ts. Add build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks to split large vendor libraries: (a) 'react-vendor': ['react', 'react-dom', 'react-router-dom']. (b) 'query-vendor': ['@tanstack/react-query']. (c) 'chart-vendor': ['recharts']. This prevents a single vendor bundle from exceeding 500 KB.
acceptance_criteria: backend/core/pagination.py SafePageNumberPagination class exists and is set as DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS
ExportCSVView enforces max row limit with clear error message
frontend/src/App.tsx uses React.lazy() for all page imports except DashboardPage/LoginPage/RegisterPage
At least 3 search-input pages use useDebounce (menu, inventory, crm customers)
At least 3 components wrapped in React.memo (MenuItemCard, KitchenOrderCard, NotificationBell)
frontend/src/main.tsx QueryClient config sets staleTime=30000 and refetchOnWindowFocus=false
frontend/vite.config.ts has build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks splitting react, query, chart vendors
cd frontend && npm run build succeeds with no TypeScript errors
cd frontend && npm run lint returns zero warnings
